entries.unit: The Tail at Scale — secondary summary

mechanism.owner_quote: A **hedged request** sends an additional equivalent read to another viable replica when an earlier attempt appears unexpectedly slow, then uses an acceptable response and cancels remaining attempts.
mechanism.reason: Defines the trigger, replica choice, response selection and cancellation.

invariant.owner_quote: Hedge delayed reads | Equivalent replicas; bounded speculative budget; cancellation; measured independent tails | Shared bottleneck, expensive writes, inconsistent replicas
invariant.reason: Lists the required preconditions and contraindications for hedging.

failure_recovery.owner_quote: Hedging can double work exactly when a shared dependency is saturated; it also risks duplicate side effects if the read is not truly equivalent.
failure_recovery.reason: Names the doubled-work and duplicate-effect failure modes.

alternative.owner_quote: Retry with jitter, improve the slow path, or parallelize truly independent reads may be preferable when replicas share a bottleneck or the operation is not safely repeatable.
alternative.reason: Names the competing mitigations and reversal condition.

mechanism.owner_quote: A startup probe answers "has initialization finished"; readiness answers "may this instance receive new work"; liveness answers "must the process be restarted".
mechanism.reason: Defines the mechanism and its scope.

invariant.owner_quote: They must not be collapsed into one endpoint.

failure_recovery.owner_quote: A shared dependency failure can fail every probe and cause mass ejection or restart; a cached "healthy" answer can keep sending traffic to a draining instance.
failure_recovery.reason: Names the failure and recovery response.

alternative.owner_quote: Synthetic checks or SLO-based external monitoring may be preferable when the runtime probe cannot observe the user journey.
alternative.reason: Names the competing choice and reversal.

sections: 26.2.3. Preparing the Primary for Standby Servers

mechanism.owner_quote: Failover moves authority from region A to a surviving region B under an explicit decision; failback is a second migration from B back to A, not the inverse operation.
mechanism.reason: Defines the mechanism and its scope.

invariant.owner_quote: Quarantine A, reconcile any divergent writes under one selected authority, verify user journeys, then reintroduce A as a replica or standby before considering promotion.

failure_recovery.owner_quote: A failback that merely points DNS back can resurrect stale writes and split authority.
failure_recovery.reason: Names the failure and recovery response.

alternative.owner_quote: Stay on the promoted region and rebuild the old region as a standby when failback risk exceeds its benefit.
alternative.reason: Names the competing choice and reversal.
